en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: An Islamic commercial bank is establishing a new Shari'ah governance structure. The Board of Directors suggests appointing two senior Fiqh scholars as the core Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSto ensure agility in decision-making. According to AAOIFI GS 19, which of the following statements is correct regarding this composition?
en.A: The setup is fully compliant, provided both appointed scholars possess at least 15 years of practical experience in Fiqh Al-Muamalat.
en.B: The setup is non-compliant because the SSB must consist of at least three Shari'ah scholars specialised in Fiqh Al-Muamalat.
en.C: The setup is compliant if the bank additionally appoints a senior financial market advisor to assist the board with technical matters.
en.D: The setup is non-compliant unless it receives prior written approval from the shareholders during an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM).
en.True answer: The setup is non-compliant because the SSB must consist of at least three Shari'ah scholars specialised in Fiqh Al-Muamalat.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 7-band ("Each institution shall have an SSB consisting of at least three Shari'ah scholars specialised in Fiqh Al-Muamalat...").

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution (IFI) wants to appoint a Fintech specialist who holds a master's degree in Computer Science but has no formal degree in Islamic jurisprudence. The management wants to assign this specialist as an SSB advisor. Under GS 19, how is this proposed appointment evaluated?
en.A: Invalid, because all members and advisors serving the SSB are required to hold a formal master's degree in Islamic jurisprudence or Fiqh.
en.B: Valid, provided the Fintech specialist is granted full voting rights on all board resolutions concerning digital financial products.
en.C: Valid, provided the individual is a Muslim, a recognized expert in their field, and possesses a basic understanding of Shari'ah principles.
en.D: Invalid, because GS 19 strictly prohibits individuals without a finance or legal background from serving as advisors in any capacity.
en.True answer: Valid, provided the individual is a Muslim, a recognized expert in their field, and possesses a basic understanding of Shari'ah principles.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: The Board of Directors (acting as Those Charged with Governance - TCWG) of an Islamic Bank directly signs an executive resolution to appoint three SSB members and fix their compensation packages without presenting it to shareholders. According to GS 19, what is the status of this procedure?
en.A: Fully valid, because TCWG holds full executive mandate to execute corporate governance appointments without shareholder intervention.
en.B: Valid, provided the Regulatory and Supervisory Authority issues a formal post-facto ratification letter within 30 days of appointment.
en.C: Invalid, because only the Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RSpossesses the legal power to select and appoint SSB scholars.
en.D: Invalid, because SSB members must be approved by shareholders in their general meeting upon the recommendation of TCWG.
en.True answer: Invalid, because SSB members must be approved by shareholders in their general meeting upon the recommendation of TCWG.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 12-band ("SSB members shall be approved by the shareholders of the institution in their general meeting at the recommendation of TCWG").

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: An Islamic bank experiences an emergency where all previous SSB members resign simultaneously. The bank fails to appoint a new SSB within the timeframe mandated by the local banking authority. According to AAOIFI GS 19, what action may the Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RStake?
en.A: Revoke the operating license of the Islamic bank immediately and initiate compulsory liquidation proceedings.
en.B: Order the automatic conversion of the institution into a conventional commercial bank with immediate effect.
en.C: Appoint a temporary SSB at its discretion, with all associated costs borne directly by the institution.
en.D: Require the Chief Risk Officer and Internal Shari'ah Auditor to jointly assume all duties of the SSB temporarily.
en.True answer: Appoint a temporary SSB at its discretion, with all associated costs borne directly by the institution.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 15-band ("The RSA, at its discretion, may appoint a temporary SSB if an institution fails to appoint an SSB within the time stipulated by the RSThe cost... shall be borne by the institution").

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: An Islamic window of an international bank intends to draft engagement contracts for its newly selected SSB members. What are the contractual term duration requirements specified in AAOIFI GS 19?
en.A: Indefinite term contracts to guarantee complete operational independence from executive management influence.
en.B: One-year renewable performance contracts subject to annual evaluation by the Board Audit Committee.
en.C: Contracts for service with a minimum term of three years and a maximum term of five years.
en.D: Ten-year non-renewable fixed terms to ensure long-term stability in Shari'ah governance oversight.
en.True answer: Contracts for service with a minimum term of three years and a maximum term of five years.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 16-band ("...contract for service for a minimum term of three years but no longer than five years").

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: To assess the "Fit and Proper" criteria for appointing a Shari'ah scholar to the SSB, an institution reviews several candidates. Which candidate's profile meets the minimum requirements established under AAOIFI GS 19?
en.A: Candidate A: Holds a Master's degree in Fiqh, has 12 years of experience in Fiqh Al-Muamalat, and is fluent in Arabic and local business language.
en.B: Candidate B: Holds a Bachelor's degree in Economics and possesses 2 years of operational experience in Islamic banking window operations.
en.C: Candidate C: A non-Muslim legal scholar with 20 years of research experience in Middle Eastern commercial law frameworks.
en.D: Candidate D: A Shari'ah scholar holding a Ph.who publicly advocates opinions directly contradicting established scholarly consensus (Ijma).
en.True answer: Candidate A: Holds a Master's degree in Fiqh, has 12 years of experience in Fiqh Al-Muamalat, and is fluent in Arabic and local business language.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 18-band (Muslim, Master's degree or above in Shari'ah/Fiqh, at least 10 years of experience in Fiqh Al-Muamalat, good command of Arabic and business language, and not holding anomalous opinions contradicting consensus).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: An SSB scholar missed all scheduled quarterly meetings of an Islamic bank during the financial year without providing any valid reason or reasonable excuse. According to AAOIFI GS 19, what governance consequence applies?
en.A: The scholar's annual fee is automatically reduced by 50%, but membership on the board remains active.
en.B: The scholar becomes subject to potential disqualification for unexcused meeting absenteeism.
en.C: The CEO gains unilateral authority to issue a formal reprimand and extend the term of appointment.
en.D: No formal disciplinary consequence applies as long as the scholar signs the annual Shari'ah report at year-end.
en.True answer: The scholar becomes subject to potential disqualification for unexcused meeting absenteeism.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 21(band (Disqualification criteria: "fails to attend the minimum number of meetings in a year without a reasonable excuse").

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Which of the following describes the hierarchy of "Shari'ah principles and rules" defined under AAOIFI GS 19 when assessing compliance or resolving ambiguities?
en.A: Central Bank regulations > Local custom (Urf) > AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards > Internal SSB rulings.
en.B: Management executive resolutions > Internal SSB rulings > AAOIFI Standards > International Financial Reporting Standards.
en.C: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards > Regulatory requirements > Central Board rulings > AAOIFI FAS > Institution SSB rulings.
en.D: Internal SSB rulings of the institution always override national regulatory Shari'ah board rulings without exception.
en.True answer: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards > Regulatory requirements > Central Board rulings > AAOIFI FAS > Institution SSB rulings.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 5(band (Hierarchy of Shari'ah principles and rules: i. AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards; ii. Regulatory Shari'ah requirements; iii. Central Shari'ah board rulings; iv. AAOIFI FAS Shari'ah requirements; v. SSB rulings).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question:
An IFI aims to ensure diversity in its SSB composition to enhance governance quality. According to AAOIFI GS 19, which elements should preferably be reflected in the SSB composition?

i. Representation from different legal schools of thought (Madhahiin the country.
ii. Representation of different fields of technical expertise relevant to Islamic finance.
iii. Inclusion of both senior and junior scholars.
en.A: i only
en.B: i and ii only
en.C: ii and iii only
en.D: i, ii, and iii
en.True answer: i, ii, and iii

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under AAOIFI GS 19, which of the following actions constitutes a valid ground for the disqualification of an active SSB member?
en.A: The member expresses a dissenting opinion during an internal meeting regarding a proposed Sukuk structure.
en.B: The member misuses confidential client information for personal benefit or to harm the bank's competitive standing.
en.C: The member publishes an academic journal article analyzing classical jurisprudence views on modern derivatives.
en.D: The member advises executive management to increase the bank's annual allocation to charitable endowment funds.
en.True answer: The member misuses confidential client information for personal benefit or to harm the bank's competitive standing.
en.main: Asos: AAOIFI GS 19, 21(g) band (Disqualification: "misuses confidential and privileged information about the institution or its clients... for personal benefit or in a manner that is detrimental to competitive interests").

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor is finalising the report of an Islamic financial institution. Management has prepared the financial statements and has also undertaken to operate the institution in accordance with Shari’a Rules and Principles. Which statement should appear in the introductory paragraph?
en.A: Management is responsible for preparing the financial statements, while the auditor is responsible for ensuring Shari’a compliance in all operations.
en.B: Management is responsible for the financial statements and its undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari’a Rules and Principles, while the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion based on the audit.
en.C: Management is responsible for the financial statements, while the Shari’a Supervisory Board is responsible for expressing an audit opinion based on the auditor’s procedures.
en.D: Management is responsible for the financial statements and accounting policies, while the auditor is responsible for determining whether management has complied with all Shari’a requirements.
en.True answer: Management is responsible for the financial statements and its undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari’a Rules and Principles, while the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion based on the audit.
en.main: ASIFI - 2: 9. The report should include a statement that the financial statements and the financial institution's undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari'a Rules and Principles are the responsibility of the financial institution's management, and a statement that the responsibility of the auditor is to express an opinion on the financial statements based on the audit. (Consideration should be given to the definition of management in relevant national legislation and regulations.)

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor is drafting the scope paragraph for an Islamic financial institution operating in a country with its own auditing practices. Which description most appropriately reflects the requirements of ASIFI 2?
en.A: The audit was conducted in accordance with AAOIFI accounting standards and relevant national practices, provided that those practices are consistent with the financial institution’s internal policies.
en.B: The audit was conducted in accordance with ASIFIs and relevant national standards or practices, as appropriate, provided that they do not contravene Shari’a Rules and Principles.
en.C: The audit was conducted in accordance with the national auditing standards applicable to the auditor, together with any accounting standards issued by the Shari’a Supervisory Board.
en.D: The audit was conducted in accordance with international auditing standards and relevant national legislation, provided that management considers those standards appropriate for the institution.
en.True answer: The audit was conducted in accordance with ASIFIs and relevant national standards or practices, as appropriate, provided that they do not contravene Shari’a Rules and Principles.
en.main: ASIFI -2: 12. The report needs to explain the scope of the audit. It should state that the examination was performed following ASIFIs as well as relevant national standards or practices, provided they do not conflict with Shari'a Rules and Principles. "Scope" means the auditor's capacity to carry out the required auditing tasks under specific circumstances. This gives readers confidence that the review followed established professional guidelines. Unless specified otherwise, the applied national auditing standards are assumed to belong to the country where the auditor's office is located.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: During the preparation of the audit report, the auditor is deciding how to describe the work performeWhich statement most appropriately reflects the audit procedures required to be described in the report?
en.A: The audit included reviewing every transaction, verifying every accounting entry, reassessing all management decisions, and confirming every financial statement disclosure.
en.B: The audit included examining significant transactions, approving management estimates, reviewing internal policies, and evaluating the institution’s overall financial performance.
en.C: The audit included confirming all material balances, reviewing every accounting policy, testing all transactions, and assessing the institution’s compliance with statutory requirements.
en.D: The audit included examining evidence on a test basis, assessing accounting principles and significant estimates, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.
en.True answer: The audit included examining evidence on a test basis, assessing accounting principles and significant estimates, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.
en.main: Paragraph 14 — The report should describe the audit as including examination of evidence on a test basis, assessment of accounting principles and significant management estimates, and evaluation of overall financial statement presentation.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution prepares its financial statements under an identified financial reporting framework. After completing the audit, the auditor concludes that the statements present a true and fair view under that framework. Which opinion should normally be expressed?
en.A: A qualified opinion should be expressed because the auditor must identify every accounting judgement made by management in the report.
en.B: An adverse opinion should be expressed because management remains responsible for the preparation of the financial statements.
en.C: An unqualified opinion should be expressed because the financial statements give a true and fair view under the identified financial reporting framework.
en.D: A disclaimer of opinion should be expressed because an auditor cannot provide assurance regarding management’s accounting estimates and judgements.
en.True answer: An unqualified opinion should be expressed because the financial statements give a true and fair view under the identified financial reporting framework.
en.main: Paragraph 27 — An unqualified opinion should be expressed when the auditor concludes that the financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with the identified financial reporting framework.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor completes all necessary audit procedures on 20 March. Management signs the financial statements on 24 March. The auditor proposes dating the report 20 March because the audit work was completed on that date. What should the auditor do?
en.A: Date the report 20 March because the audit procedures were completed before management signed the financial statements.
en.B: Date the report 24 March because the auditor should not date the report earlier than the date the financial statements are signed or approved by management.
en.C: Date the report 20 March because the auditor’s reporting responsibility begins when sufficient audit evidence has been obtained.
en.D: Date the report 24 March only if management requests the later date to ensure consistency with the financial reporting period.
en.True answer: Date the report 24 March because the auditor should not date the report earlier than the date the financial statements are signed or approved by management.
en.main: Paragraph 24 — The auditor should not date the report earlier than the date on which the financial statements are signed or approved by management.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution has disclosed a significant uncertainty concerning a legal matter. The uncertainty does not relate to a going concern problem, and its eventual resolution depends on future events. The auditor considers the matter important for users of the financial statements. What may the auditor do?
en.A: Add an emphasis of matter paragraph to draw attention to the uncertainty without modifying the auditor’s opinion.
en.B: Express a qualified opinion because every significant uncertainty requires modification of the auditor’s opinion.
en.C: Express an adverse opinion because the outcome of the uncertainty depends on events occurring after the reporting date.
en.D: Express a disclaimer because the auditor cannot determine the ultimate outcome of the uncertainty at the reporting date.
en.True answer: Add an emphasis of matter paragraph to draw attention to the uncertainty without modifying the auditor’s opinion.
en.main: Paragraph 32 — The auditor should consider modifying the report by adding an emphasis of matter paragraph when there is a significant uncertainty, other than a going concern problem, whose resolution depends on future events and which may affect the financial statements. Paragraph 30 states that such an emphasis does not affect the auditor’s opinion.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution faces a material going concern problem, and the matter is appropriately disclosed in the financial statements. The auditor considers the matter significant for users of the report. What reporting treatment is specifically contemplated by ASIFI 2?
en.A: The auditor should add an emphasis of matter paragraph to highlight the material going concern problem.
en.B: The auditor should automatically issue an adverse opinion because the institution’s future operations remain uncertain.
en.C: The auditor should automatically issue a disclaimer because the institution may be unable to continue its operations.
en.D: The auditor should issue an unqualified opinion without additional explanation because the matter is already disclosed.
en.True answer: The auditor should add an emphasis of matter paragraph to highlight the material going concern problem.
en.main: Paragraph 31 — The auditor should modify the auditor’s report by adding a paragraph to highlight a material matter regarding a going concern problem. Paragraph 34 notes that in extreme cases involving multiple significant uncertainties, a disclaimer may instead be considered.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence because a scope limitation affects matters that are so material and pervasive that the auditor cannot form an opinion on the financial statements. Which reporting outcome is appropriate?
en.A: A qualified opinion should be issued because the limitation affects only the auditor’s ability to obtain sufficient evidence.
en.B: An adverse opinion should be issued because the absence of evidence indicates that the financial statements are misleading.
en.C: A disclaimer of opinion should be issued because the limitation prevents the auditor from obtaining sufficient appropriate audit evidence.
en.D: An unqualified opinion with an emphasis of matter paragraph should be issued because the limitation can be explained to users.
en.True answer: A disclaimer of opinion should be issued because the limitation prevents the auditor from obtaining sufficient appropriate audit evidence.
en.main: Paragraph 38 — A disclaimer of opinion should be expressed when the possible effect of a limitation on scope is so material and pervasive that the auditor has not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence and is therefore unable to express an opinion.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor disagrees with management over the acceptability of an accounting policy. The resulting effect on the financial statements is material, but it is not sufficiently pervasive to make the financial statements misleading as a whole. Which opinion is appropriate?
en.A: An unqualified opinion should be issued because the disagreement relates only to an accounting policy selected by management.
en.B: A qualified opinion should be issued, expressed as “except for” the effects of the matter to which the qualification relates.
en.C: An adverse opinion should be issued because any material disagreement with management prevents the auditor from expressing an unqualified opinion.
en.D: A disclaimer of opinion should be issued because the auditor cannot determine whether management’s accounting policy is appropriate.
en.True answer: A qualified opinion should be issued, expressed as “except for” the effects of the matter to which the qualification relates.
en.main: Paragraph 37 — A qualified opinion should be expressed when an unqualified opinion cannot be expressed but the effect of the disagreement is not so material and pervasive as to require an adverse opinion.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor disagrees with management regarding the implementation of Shari’a Rules and Principles as determined by the institution’s Shari’a BoarThe matter has a material effect on the financial statements. Which statement best reflects the Standard?
en.A: Such a disagreement is outside the auditor’s reporting responsibilities because Shari’a matters are determined exclusively by the Shari’a Board.
en.B: Such a disagreement may prevent an unqualified opinion and may lead to either a qualified or adverse opinion depending on its effect.
en.C: Such a disagreement automatically requires a disclaimer because the auditor cannot challenge a determination made by the Shari’a Board.
en.D: Such a disagreement requires an emphasis of matter paragraph because Shari’a matters cannot affect the auditor’s opinion on financial statements.
en.True answer: Such a disagreement may prevent an unqualified opinion and may lead to either a qualified or adverse opinion depending on its effect.
en.main: Paragraph 36(— A disagreement may concern the implementation of Shari’a Rules and Principles as determined by the Shari’a BoarIf material, it may lead to a qualified or adverse opinion.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: Management refuses to provide access to certain accounting records. The auditor believes the records are necessary, but reasonable alternative audit procedures allow sufficient appropriate evidence to be obtaineWhat should the auditor attempt to do before modifying the opinion?
en.A: Issue a qualified opinion immediately because management has restricted access to accounting records during the audit.
en.B: Issue a disclaimer immediately because management-imposed restrictions prevent the auditor from relying on the accounting records.
en.C: Accept management’s restriction and issue an unqualified opinion because the auditor remains responsible only for available evidence.
en.D: Apply reasonable alternative procedures in order to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence supporting an unqualified opinion.
en.True answer: Apply reasonable alternative procedures in order to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence supporting an unqualified opinion.
en.main: Paragraph 42 — Where a scope limitation arises from circumstances such as inadequate accounting records or inability to perform a desired procedure, the auditor should attempt reasonable alternative procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence supporting an unqualified opinion.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: A proposed audit engagement includes a contractual restriction preventing the auditor from performing a procedure considered necessary. The auditor believes the restriction would require a disclaimer of opinion. What is the normal response under ASIFI 2?
en.A: Accept the engagement and issue a disclaimer because any scope limitation can be addressed through appropriate wording in the final report.
en.B: Accept the engagement and issue a qualified opinion because a disclaimer should only be used after the audit has been completed.
en.C: Normally not accept the engagement as an audit engagement unless acceptance is required by statute and the limitation does not infringe statutory duties.
en.D: Accept the engagement and remove the restricted procedure from the audit plan because management has authority to determine the scope of the engagement.
en.True answer: Normally not accept the engagement as an audit engagement unless acceptance is required by statute and the limitation does not infringe statutory duties.
en.main: Paragraph 41 — When a proposed engagement contains a limitation that would require a disclaimer, the auditor would usually not accept it as an audit engagement unless required by statute. A statutory auditor would also not accept it where the limitation infringes statutory duties.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor must issue a qualified opinion because of a material scope limitation. Which additional information should the auditor include in the report?
en.A: The report should describe the limitation and indicate the possible adjustments that might have been necessary had the limitation not existed.
en.B: The report should describe the limitation and state that management is solely responsible for any resulting uncertainty in the financial statements.
en.C: The report should omit the limitation and instead refer users to the institution’s internal audit report for further information.
en.D: The report should describe the limitation and automatically state that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view.
en.True answer: The report should describe the limitation and indicate the possible adjustments that might have been necessary had the limitation not existed.
en.main: Paragraph 43 — When a scope limitation requires a qualified or disclaimer opinion, the report should describe the limitation and indicate the possible adjustments to the financial statements that might have been necessary had the limitation not existed.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution applies an accounting policy that the auditor considers inappropriate. The resulting effect is material and pervasive, and the auditor concludes that a qualification would not adequately describe the misleading or incomplete nature of the financial statements. Which opinion should be expressed?
en.A: A qualified opinion should be expressed because the disagreement concerns an accounting policy applied by management.
en.B: An emphasis of matter paragraph should be added because the accounting policy is already disclosed in the financial statements.
en.C: An adverse opinion should be expressed because the effect of the disagreement is so material and pervasive that qualification is inadequate.
en.D: A disclaimer of opinion should be expressed because the auditor cannot accept responsibility for management’s choice of accounting policy.
en.True answer: An adverse opinion should be expressed because the effect of the disagreement is so material and pervasive that qualification is inadequate.
en.main: Paragraph 39 — An adverse opinion should be expressed when the effect of a disagreement is so material and pervasive that a qualification is not adequate to disclose the misleading or incomplete nature of the financial statements.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor issues an opinion other than an unqualified opinion because of a material matter affecting the financial statements. Which reporting requirement applies to the auditor?
en.A: The auditor should identify the matter briefly but is not normally required to explain its possible financial effect on the financial statements.
en.B: The auditor should provide a clear description of the substantive reasons and, unless impracticable, quantify the possible effects on the financial statements.
en.C: The auditor should provide only a reference to the relevant financial statement note because users can obtain the remaining information from management.
en.D: The auditor should describe the matter in detail only when issuing an adverse opinion, while qualified opinions require only the modified opinion wording.
en.True answer: The auditor should provide a clear description of the substantive reasons and, unless impracticable, quantify the possible effects on the financial statements.
en.main: Paragraph 40 — Whenever the auditor expresses an opinion other than unqualified, the report should contain a clear description of all substantive reasons and, unless impracticable, a quantification of the possible effects on the financial statements.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: Senior management of an Islamic financial institution (IF) undertakes the evaluation of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board and submits the results to the Board of Directors for consideration. Under the Shari'ah Governance Framework, how should this arrangement be evaluated?
en.A: It constitutes a breach because the evaluation of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board is the responsibility of those charged with governance.
en.B: It is acceptable if the Board of Directors reviews and approves the evaluation.
en.C: It is acceptable if the Shari'ah Supervisory Board gives a consent to their evaluation process.
en.D: It constitutes a breach because the Shari'ah Supervisory Board should not be subject to any form of evaluation.
en.True answer: It constitutes a breach because the evaluation of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board is the responsibility of those charged with governance.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 44-paragraf — Baholash TCWG tomonidan amalga oshirilishi kerak, ijrochi rahbariyat (senior management) tomonidan o'tkazilishi taqiqlanadi).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution that is not classified as a public interest entity establishes an internal Shari'ah audit function but does not appoint an external Shari'ah auditor. Under the Shari'ah governance framework, how should this arrangement be evaluated?
en.A: It is not permissible because external Shari'ah audit is mandatory for all Islamic financial institutions.
en.B: It is permissible as external Shari'ah audit is recommended but not mandatory for institutions that are not public interest entities.
en.C: It is not permissible because internal Shari'ah audit cannot provide reliable assurance.
en.D: It is permissible only with specific approval from the regulatory authority.
en.True answer: It is permissible as external Shari'ah audit is recommended but not mandatory for institutions that are not public interest entities.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 56-paragraf — Tashqi Shari'at auditi jamoat manfaati subyektlari (public interest entities) uchun 3 yildan so'ng majburiy bo'ladi, boshqa tashkilotlar uchun esa tavsiya etiladi).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution encounters a difference between a ruling issued by its Shari'ah Supervisory Board and Shari'ah guidelines issued by the relevant regulatory authority. No specific AAOIFI Shari'ah standard addresses the matter. According to the hierarchy of Shari'ah rules, how should this matter be resolved?
en.A: The institution should comply with the regulatory authority's Shari'ah guidelines.
en.B: The institution should follow the ruling of its Shari'ah Supervisory Board.
en.C: The institution may adopt either position based on commercial considerations.
en.D: The institution should defer the matter until a relevant standard is issued.
en.True answer: The institution should comply with the regulatory authority's Shari'ah guidelines.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 4(l)-paragraf — Shari'at qoidalari iyerarxiyasida tartib berilgan: AAOIFI standartlari -> Regulyator talablari -> Markaziy Shari'at kengashi -> AAOIFI FAS -> Tashkilot SSBsi).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: A Takaful operator prepares its financial statements and omits disclosure of a Qard Hasan extended to the participants' fund to cover a deficit. Under the Shari'ah governance and disclosure requirements, how should this omission be evaluated?
en.A: It is acceptable if the matter is disclosed internally within the institution.
en.B: It constitutes a breach because Qard Hasan is not permitted in Takaful operations.
en.C: It is acceptable if disclosure may adversely affect the institution's financial position or reputation.
en.D: It constitutes a breach because relevant information relating to Qard Hasan must be disclosed in the financial statements.
en.True answer: It constitutes a breach because relevant information relating to Qard Hasan must be disclosed in the financial statements.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 81(va 81(c)-paragraflari — Takaful faoliyatida Qard Hasan bo'yicha ma'lumotlarni ochiqlash majburiydir).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution discontinues its internal Shari'ah Supervisory Board and relies solely on rulings issued by the central Shari'ah authority for compliance purposes. Under the Shari'ah governance framework, how should this arrangement be evaluated?
en.A: It is acceptable because central Shari'ah rulings replace institutional Shari'ah governance functions.
en.B: It is acceptable if the institution obtains direct oversight from the central Shari'ah authority.
en.C: It is not acceptable because internal Shari'ah governance functions remain the responsibility of the institution.
en.D: It is acceptable if external Shari'ah audit is implemented in place of internal supervision.
en.True answer: It is not acceptable because internal Shari'ah governance functions remain the responsibility of the institution.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 8-paragraf va 5-Prinsip — Har bir muassasa o'zining ichki Shari'at boshqaruvi organlariga (SSB, compliance, internal audit) ega bo'lishi shart).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: To manage its limited budget during its first year of operations, a newly licensed Islamic retail bank officially outsources both its internal Shari'ah audit and its day-to-day Shari'ah Compliance Department (SCfunctions to a reputable external advisory firm, arguing that this guarantees maximum independence from internal pressure. Based on the governance framework for the compliance function, how is the bank's decision to outsource the SCD evaluated?
en.A: It is permissible only if the external advisory firm is completely independent of the bank's Shari'ah Supervisory Board to avoid any self-review threat.
en.B: It is unacceptable because the compliance function is an internal management responsibility that inherently cannot be delegated to third parties.
en.C: It is a valid strategy for newly established or smaller banks, provided the external firm's Shari'ah compliance manual is approved by the bank's board of directors.
en.D: It is only permissible if the bank's internal Shari'ah audit team continues to perform the ex-post detective controls while the external firm handles the ex-ante preventive controls.
en.True answer: It is unacceptable because the compliance function is an internal management responsibility that inherently cannot be delegated to third parties.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 32 va 47-paragraflari — Shari'at muvofiqligi (compliance) va uning nazorati ijrochi rahbariyatning ichki mas'uliyati hisoblanadi).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: The CEO of an Islamic financial institution is restructuring the organization and decides to merge the product development team directly into the Shari'ah Compliance Department (SCto speed up the launch of new financing apps, mandating that the Head of the SCD will now officially report only to the Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSto ensure total religious independence. Considering the structural and reporting requirements for the compliance unit, what makes the CEO's restructuring technically invalid?
en.A: The SCD is fundamentally a management function that must report to senior management and allowing it to actively develop products creates an inherent self-review threat.
en.B: The SCD must report primarily to the risk management committee, and merging it with product development violates the specific mandate of the central Shari'ah board.
en.C: The SCD is required to be structurally independent from the SSB to act as a proper check and balance, meaning a direct reporting line to the scholars is strictly prohibited.
en.D: The SCD is an ex-post detective control organ, making it incompatible with the ex-ante preventive nature of designing and launching new financial products.
en.True answer: The SCD is fundamentally a management function that must report to senior management and allowing it to actively develop products creates an inherent self-review threat.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 48(a)-paragraf — SCD mahsuldorlik/boshqaruv funksiyasi hisoblanib, ijrochi rahbariyatga hisobdor va o'z faoliyatida manfaatlar to'qnashuvi / self-review xavfidan xoli bo'lishi kerak).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: An Islamic financial institution assigns the secretariat function of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board to an employee who also performs Shari'ah compliance duties within management. Under the Shari'ah governance framework, when is such an arrangement permissible?
en.A: When the individual performs secretariat duties under the direct oversight of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board and appropriate safeguards are in place to maintain independence.
en.B: When the institution lacks sufficient resources to appoint a separate secretariat function.
en.C: When the Shari'ah Supervisory Board approves the arrangement regardless of reporting structure.
en.D: When the individual avoids reviewing matters previously handled by the compliance function.
en.True answer: When the individual performs secretariat duties under the direct oversight of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board and appropriate safeguards are in place to maintain independence.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 51(k)-paragraf — Katibiyat (Secretariat) vazifasini Shari'at muvofiqligi bo'limiga yuklash SSB roziligi va tegishli mustaqillik choralarini ko'rish sharti bilan ruxsat etiladi).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: A large Islamic financial institution integrates its internal Shari'ah audit function into the internal audit department. Under the Shari'ah governance framework, how should this arrangement be evaluated?
en.A: It is not permissible because internal audit functions cannot perform Shari'ah-related assessments.
en.B: It is not appropriate because such integration is only acceptable in limited cases, such as smaller institutions or less developed environments.
en.C: It is permissible if the head of internal audit meets Shari'ah fit and proper requirements.
en.D: It is not permissible unless the function is outsourced to an external party.
en.True answer: It is not appropriate because such integration is only acceptable in limited cases, such as smaller institutions or less developed environments.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 62-paragraf — Proporsionalik tamoyiliga ko'ra birlashtirish faqat kichik muassasalar yoki rivojlanayotgan muhitlarda ruxsat etiladi).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: A large conventional banking group operates a standalone Islamic finance window. The group's executives argue that because the window is not a separate legal entity, it should not be subjected to a rigorous, independent external Shari'ah audit. How does the AAOIFI auditing standards evaluate this claim?
en.A: The executives are correct, as external Shari'ah audit requirements are generally applied to legally incorporated Islamic financial institutions, and not to internal divisions that operate under the same legal identity as the parent bank.
en.B: The claim is not appropriate, as Islamic windows and standalone branches are expected to be subject to the same level of independent external Shari'ah audit and oversight, given that Shari'ah compliance applies to the nature of activities rather than the legal form of the entity.
en.C: The claim is acceptable provided the parent bank undergoes a comprehensive statutory financial audit, as this would indirectly ensure that the Islamic window's operations are reviewed within the overall audit framework of the parent bank.
en.D: The claim may be accepted where the Islamic window maintains internal Shari'ah review mechanisms and proper segregation of funds, as these controls can sufficiently mitigate the need for a full external Shari'ah audit if the parent bank is audited by an external auditor.
en.True answer: The claim is not appropriate, as Islamic windows and standalone branches are expected to be subject to the same level of independent external Shari'ah audit and oversight, given that Shari'ah compliance applies to the nature of activities rather than the legal form of the entity.
en.main: (Asos: GS 1, 2, 4(va 14-paragraflari — Standart talablari Islomiy darchalar (Islamic windows) uchun ham to'liq va teng darajada amal qiladi).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: During the audit of Al-Rayan Islamic Bank, the external auditor finds that management has not charged depreciation on assets acquired for operating Ijarah, contrary to AAOIFI accounting standards. Management refuses to correct this. The effect is material to total assets and net income, but all other balances and disclosures are fairly stateUnder ASIFI 2, what type of report should the auditor issue?
en.A: An unqualified opinion with an emphasis of matter paragraph drawing attention to the depreciation policy
en.B: A qualified 'except for' opinion, with a separate paragraph before the opinion describing the matter and quantifying its effect
en.C: An adverse opinion, because management has refused to correct a departure from AAOIFI standards
en.D: A disclaimer of opinion, because the auditor cannot rely on management's representations
en.True answer: A qualified 'except for' opinion, with a separate paragraph before the opinion describing the matter and quantifying its effect
en.main: Paras 36(b), 37 and 45: a material disagreement with management on accounting policies leads to a qualified or adverse opinion. Since the effect is material but NOT pervasive, a qualified opinion expressed as 'except for' is appropriate (para 37). Para 40 requires a clear description of the reasons and, unless impracticable, quantification of the effect, usually in a separate paragraph preceding the opinion (see the depreciation illustration in para 46). An emphasis of matter cannot be used, as it does not address a misstatement.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: The auditor of an Islamic bank concludes that management has recognised the entire profit on long-term deferred Murabaha transactions at inception, has presented unrestricted investment accounts within owners' equity, and has omitted the disclosure of significant non-Shari'a-compliant earnings required by the Shari'a Supervisory BoarManagement refuses all adjustments. The combined effect distorts most of the key figures in the financial statements. Which opinion is appropriate?
en.A: A qualified opinion listing each disagreement separately
en.B: A disclaimer of opinion, because the matters involve Shari'a rules outside the auditor's competence
en.C: An unqualified opinion with an emphasis of matter paragraph, since the matters are disclosed by management
en.D: An adverse opinion, stating that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view
en.True answer: An adverse opinion, stating that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view
en.main: Para 36(b): disagreements may concern the implementation of Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB, the acceptability of accounting policies, their application or the adequacy of disclosures; such disagreements lead to a qualified or adverse opinion. Para 39: an adverse opinion is required when the effect of the disagreement is so material and PERVASIVE that a qualification is not adequate to disclose the misleading nature of the financial statements. A disclaimer relates to scope limitations, not disagreements.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: A fire destroys the records and original contracts supporting most of an Islamic bank's Musharaka and Mudaraba financing portfolio, which represents the majority of its total assets. Counterparties do not respond to confirmation requests, and no other satisfactory audit procedures are available. How should the auditor report?
en.A: Issue a disclaimer of opinion, describe the limitation, and omit the sentence stating the auditor's responsibility to express an opinion
en.B: Issue a qualified 'except for' opinion, since the limitation was caused by circumstances rather than imposed by management
en.C: Issue an adverse opinion, because the financing portfolio cannot be supported by evidence
en.D: Issue an unqualified opinion with an emphasis of matter paragraph describing the fire
en.True answer: Issue a disclaimer of opinion, describe the limitation, and omit the sentence stating the auditor's responsibility to express an opinion
en.main: Para 38: a disclaimer is expressed when the possible effect of a scope limitation is so material and pervasive that the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence. Para 43: the report should describe the limitation and indicate possible adjustments. The disclaimer illustration in para 44 begins 'We were engaged to audit...' and OMITS the sentence on the auditor's responsibility, concluding that the auditor is unable to express an opinion. Whether the limitation is imposed by circumstances or the client does not change the outcome when its effect is pervasive.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: A newly established Islamic finance company proposes engagement terms under which the external auditor will NOT audit the company's compliance with Shari'a Rules and Principles. The auditor believes that this limitation would require a disclaimer of opinion. There is no statutory requirement for the audit. Under ASIFI 2, what is the most appropriate course of action?
en.A: Accept the engagement and issue a qualified opinion excluding Shari'a compliance from the scope
en.B: Accept the engagement, provided the Shari'a Supervisory Board confirms compliance in writing
en.C: Not accept the limited engagement as an audit engagement
en.D: Accept the engagement and include an emphasis of matter paragraph explaining the limitation
en.True answer: Not accept the limited engagement as an audit engagement
en.main: Para 41: a scope limitation may be imposed by the institution, e.g. terms specifying that the auditor will not audit compliance with Shari'a Rules and Principles. When such a limitation in a PROPOSED engagement is such that the auditor believes a disclaimer would be needed, the auditor would usually NOT accept it as an audit engagement unless required by statute; a statutory auditor would not accept it where it infringes statutory duties. An SSB confirmation cannot replace the auditor's own evidence.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An auditor is appointed to an Islamic bank two months after the year end and therefore could not attend the physical count of commodities held for Murabaha, which are material to the financial statements. What should the auditor do FIRST under ASIFI 2?
en.A: Issue a disclaimer of opinion, since a scope limitation exists over a material balance
en.B: Attempt reasonable alternative procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to support an unqualified opinion
en.C: Issue a qualified opinion, since the limitation was imposed by circumstances
en.D: Rely on the Shari'a Supervisory Board's report confirming that the commodities exist
en.True answer: Attempt reasonable alternative procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to support an unqualified opinion
en.main: Para 42: a scope limitation may be imposed by circumstances, for example when the timing of the auditor's appointment prevents observing physical counts. In such circumstances the auditor would attempt reasonable ALTERNATIVE procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to support an unqualified opinion. Only if this fails would a qualified opinion or disclaimer be considered (paras 37, 38, 43).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: An Islamic bank has breached its regulatory capital requirements and its continued operation depends on a capital injection that shareholders have not yet approveManagement has fully and appropriately disclosed this material going concern uncertainty in the notes. The auditor agrees with the accounting and disclosures. How should the auditor's report be modified?
en.A: Add an emphasis of matter paragraph, preferably after the opinion paragraph, highlighting the going concern problem and stating that the opinion is not qualified in this respect
en.B: Issue a qualified opinion, because the going concern uncertainty is material
en.C: No modification is needed, since management has adequately disclosed the matter
en.D: Issue an adverse opinion, because the bank may not continue as a going concern
en.True answer: Add an emphasis of matter paragraph, preferably after the opinion paragraph, highlighting the going concern problem and stating that the opinion is not qualified in this respect
en.main: Para 31: the auditor SHOULD modify the report by adding a paragraph to highlight a material matter regarding a going concern problem. Para 30: an emphasis of matter paragraph does not affect the opinion, is preferably placed after the opinion paragraph and ordinarily states that the opinion is not qualified in this respect. Para 34 adds that in extreme cases involving multiple significant uncertainties, a disclaimer may be considered instead.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: For the year ended 31 December 20X5, the auditor of an Islamic bank completes all fieldwork on 3 February 20X6. The board of directors approves and signs the financial statements on 10 February 20X6. The annual report is published on 20 February 20X6 and the general assembly meets on 15 March 20X6. What is the earliest date the auditor may place on the report?
en.A: 3 February 20X6, the date fieldwork was completed
en.B: 20 February 20X6, the date of publication
en.C: 10 February 20X6, the date the financial statements were approved by management
en.D: 15 March 20X6, the date of the general assembly
en.True answer: 10 February 20X6, the date the financial statements were approved by management
en.main: Para 23: the report is dated as of the completion date of the audit, informing the reader that the auditor has considered events up to that date. Para 24: since the auditor reports on financial statements as prepared and presented by management, the report should NOT be dated earlier than the date on which the financial statements are signed or approved by management. Hence 10 February 20X6 is the earliest date.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: A junior auditor drafts the opening (introductory) paragraph of an auditor's report on an Islamic bank. Which description of responsibilities is consistent with ASIFI 2?
en.A: The financial statements are the responsibility of management, while the institution's undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari'a is the responsibility of the Shari'a Supervisory Board
en.B: The financial statements are the joint responsibility of management and the auditor, who is also responsible for confirming Shari'a compliance
en.C: The financial statements are the responsibility of the board of directors, and the auditor is responsible for the institution's undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari'a
en.D: The financial statements and the institution's undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari'a Rules and Principles are the responsibility of management; the auditor's responsibility is to express an opinion based on the audit
en.True answer: The financial statements and the institution's undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari'a Rules and Principles are the responsibility of management; the auditor's responsibility is to express an opinion based on the audit
en.main: Para 9: the report should state that the financial statements AND the institution's undertaking to operate in accordance with Shari'a Rules and Principles are the responsibility of management, and that the auditor's responsibility is to express an opinion on the financial statements based on the audit (illustrated in para 11). Para 10: financial statements are management's representations, involving significant estimates and judgements.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: Under ASIFI 2, the opinion paragraph of an unqualified report on an Islamic bank should state that the financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with which of the following?
en.A: AAOIFI accounting standards only, since Shari'a compliance is reported separately by the Shari'a Supervisory Board
en.B: The Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the Shari'a Supervisory Board of the institution, and the accounting standards of AAOIFI (and, where appropriate, statutory requirements)
en.C: The Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the auditor's own Shari'a experts, and international financial reporting standards
en.D: The resolutions of the central bank's Shari'a board, which prevail over the institution's own Shari'a Supervisory Board
en.True answer: The Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the Shari'a Supervisory Board of the institution, and the accounting standards of AAOIFI (and, where appropriate, statutory requirements)
en.main: Para 17: the opinion states whether the financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with the Shari'a Rules and Principles AS DETERMINED BY THE SHARI'A SUPERVISORY BOARD of the Islamic financial institution and the financial reporting framework, and where appropriate whether they comply with statutory requirements. Paras 19 and 21: the framework is indicated by reference to AAOIFI accounting standards and relevant national requirements.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 02: Auditor’s Report
en.Question: The audited financial statements of an Islamic bank are fairly presenteHowever, the chairman's statement in the same annual report describes the bank's financing growth using figures that are materially inconsistent with the audited financial statements. Management refuses to amend the chairman's statement. How should the auditor respond under ASIFI 2?
en.A: Consider including an emphasis of matter paragraph describing the material inconsistency, without modifying the opinion on the financial statements
en.B: Issue a qualified opinion, because the annual report contains misleading information
en.C: Issue an adverse opinion, because management has refused to correct the inconsistency
en.D: Take no action, since the chairman's statement is not part of the audited financial statements
en.True answer: Consider including an emphasis of matter paragraph describing the material inconsistency, without modifying the opinion on the financial statements
en.main: Para 35: an emphasis of matter paragraph may also report on matters OTHER than those affecting the financial statements. If an amendment is necessary to other information in a document containing the audited financial statements and the institution refuses, the auditor would consider including an emphasis of matter paragraph describing the material inconsistency. Para 30: an emphasis of matter does not affect the auditor's opinion, which remains unqualified because the financial statements themselves are fairly stated.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: Which of the following is NOT part of the minimum components/organs of the Shari'ah governance framework under AAOIFI GS 1?
en.A: Shari'ah supervisory board (SSB)
en.B: Shari'ah compliance function
en.C: Central Shari'ah board (CSB)
en.D: External Shari'ah audit (ESA)
en.True answer: Central Shari'ah board (CSB)
en.main: Rationale: Paragraph 8 sets out the minimum as four organs: the SSB, the Shari'ah compliance function, the internal Shari'ah audit function and the ESUnder Principle 3 (par7), the CSB is only recommended (BC23).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: For a retail IFI to be classed as a public interest institution, the number of investment accounts, unitholders or participants must exceed which threshold, unless the RSA defines it differently?
en.main: Rationale: The explanation to par4(h)(iii) says the number is considered large if it is in excess of 10,000 unless differently defined by the respective RSA.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: How often must an external Shari'ah audit (ESbe performed?
en.A: Every six months
en.B: Annually
en.C: Every two years
en.D: Every three years
en.True answer: Annually
en.main: Rationale: Par55: an ESA shall be performed for an institution on an annual basis. The "three years" in option D is not the audit frequency. It is the transition period before ESA becomes mandatory for public interest institutions (par56).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: From which date is GS 1 (Revised 2024) effective?
en.A: 1 January 2026
en.B: 29 December 2024
en.C: 1 January 2025
en.True answer: 1 January 2026
en.main: Rationale: Par82: the standard is effective on or after 1 January 2026, and earlier application is encourage29 December 2024 is the date of final issuance, and 20 May 2024 is when AGEB approved it (Appendices A and C).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: According to the GS 1 definition, Shari'ah non-compliance risk is a sub-set of which risk?
en.A: Credit risk
en.B: Operational risk
en.C: Market risk
en.D: Liquidity risk
en.True answer: Operational risk
en.main: Rationale: Par4(k): it is a sub-set of operational risk and may in certain circumstances result in legal, financial or reputational risk.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: What is the status of the SSB's Fatwas and rulings on Shari'ah matters for the institution?
en.A: They are advisory only
en.B: They become binding only after approval by the board of directors
en.C: They are binding on the institution
en.D: They are binding only on the Shari'ah compliance department
en.True answer: They are binding on the institution
en.main: Rationale: Par4(m): the Fatwas and rulings (related to Shari'ah matters) of the SSB are binding on the institution.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: Which option correctly shows the hierarchy of Shari'ah principles and rules under GS 1 (from top to bottom)?
en.A: Institution's SSB rulings → CSB rulings → regulator's regulations → AAOIFI Shari'ah standards → AAOIFI FAS requirements
en.B: AAOIFI Shari'ah standards → regulator's regulations → CSB rulings → Shari'ah-related requirements of AAOIFI FASs → approvals and rulings of the institution's SSB
en.C: Regulator's regulations → AAOIFI Shari'ah standards → CSB rulings → institution's SSB rulings → AAOIFI FAS
en.D: AAOIFI Shari'ah standards → CSB rulings → regulator's regulations → AAOIFI FAS → institution's SSB rulings
en.True answer: AAOIFI Shari'ah standards → regulator's regulations → CSB rulings → Shari'ah-related requirements of AAOIFI FASs → approvals and rulings of the institution's SSB
en.main: Rationale: Par4(l): (i) AAOIFI Shari'ah standards, (ii) regulator's regulations, (iii) CSB rulings, (iv) Shari'ah-related requirements of AAOIFI FASs, (v) approvals and rulings of the institution's SSIf there is an ambiguity in interpreting (i) to (iv), the SSB's clarification prevails.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: Which statement correctly reflects the GS 1 requirement on assessing the performance of the SSB and each of its members?
en.A: Senior management assesses them once a year
en.B: TCWG assesses them once every three years
en.C: The Shari'ah compliance department assesses them every six months
en.D: TCWG assesses them through a formal process at least annually, and senior management cannot perform the assessment in any manner
en.True answer: TCWG assesses them through a formal process at least annually, and senior management cannot perform the assessment in any manner
en.main: Rationale: Par44: TCWG shall establish a formal process to assess the SSB and each member at a minimum annually. The explanation states that such an assessment cannot be performed by senior management in any manner whatsoever. This protects the independence of the SSB.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: Which statement about the difference between the internal Shari'ah audit function and the Shari'ah compliance function is correct?
en.A: Internal Shari'ah audit is independent of management, provides assurance to TCWG and the SSB, and assesses the adequacy and effectiveness of controls. The compliance function is an ongoing monitoring process
en.B: Internal Shari'ah audit is an ongoing monitoring process, while the compliance function assesses the adequacy of controls
en.C: Both are part of management and report directly to the CEO
en.D: Internal Shari'ah audit provides independent third-party assurance to the institution's stakeholders
en.True answer: Internal Shari'ah audit is independent of management, provides assurance to TCWG and the SSB, and assesses the adequacy and effectiveness of controls. The compliance function is an ongoing monitoring process
en.main: Rationale: Par33: internal Shari'ah audit is independent of management, with the primary objective of providing assurance to TCWG and the SSB and assessing the adequacy and effectiveness of controls. The compliance function is an ongoing process of monitoring. Independent third-party assurance (is provided by the ESA (par34).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 01: Shari'ah Governance Framework (Revised 2024)
en.Question: A retail IFI has 12,000 investment accountholders. Its shares are not listed on a stock exchange and it has not issued Sukuk. The RSA has not changed the threshold, and the standard became effective on 1 January 2026. Which conclusion is correct for the year 2027?
en.A: The IFI is not a public interest institution, so ESA will never be mandatory for it
en.B: The IFI is a public interest institution and ESA is mandatory immediately from 1 January 2026
en.C: The IFI is a public interest institution. In 2027, ESA is strongly recommended, it becomes mandatory after the three-year transition period (from 2029), and it must be performed annually
en.D: The IFI is not a public interest institution because it is not listed, so ESA is only recommended
en.True answer: The IFI is a public interest institution. In 2027, ESA is strongly recommended, it becomes mandatory after the three-year transition period (from 2029), and it must be performed annually
en.main: Rationale: Par4(h)(iii): all retail IFIs dealing with a large number of stakeholders (over 10,000) are public interest institutions. Listing or Sukuk is not required, as these are separate criteria in sub-paragraphs (i) and (ii). Par56: ESA is mandatory for public interest institutions after three years from the effective date, and strongly recommended during that perioPar55: ESA is performed annually.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: The head of internal audit at Al-Falah Islamic Bank states that ASIFI 4 governs his department's Shari'a compliance testing, so his team must follow its requirements in the same way as the external auditor. How should this statement be evaluated?
en.A: It is correct, because ASIFI 4 applies to any function that tests Shari'a compliance within the IFI
en.B: It is incorrect, because for the purposes of ASIFI 4 the term 'auditor' refers to the external auditor only and does not apply to any internal audit function of the IFI
en.C: It is correct only if the internal audit department reports directly to the Shari'a Supervisory Board
en.D: It is incorrect, because ASIFI 4 applies only to the Shari'a Supervisory Board's own review work
en.True answer: It is incorrect, because for the purposes of ASIFI 4 the term 'auditor' refers to the external auditor only and does not apply to any internal audit function of the IFI
en.main: Para 2: for the purposes of ASIFI 4, 'auditor' refers to the EXTERNAL auditor only and does not apply to any internal audit function that may be associated with the IFI. Para 1: the standard deals with Shari'a compliance testing in connection with the audit of the financial statements.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: When testing an Islamic bank's compliance with Shari'a Rules and Principles, what level of assurance and evidence is the external auditor required to obtain under ASIFI 4?
en.A: Absolute assurance that every transaction during the year complied with Shari'a Rules and Principles
en.B: Limited assurance based mainly on management's representations
en.C: Reasonable assurance that the IFI complied with Shari'a Rules and Principles according to the auditor's own interpretation of Shari'a
en.D: Sufficient appropriate audit evidence providing reasonable assurance that the IFI has complied with Shari'a Rules and Principles, meaning the transactions examined comply with them as determined by the IFI's Shari'a Supervisory Board
en.True answer: Sufficient appropriate audit evidence providing reasonable assurance that the IFI has complied with Shari'a Rules and Principles, meaning the transactions examined comply with them as determined by the IFI's Shari'a Supervisory Board
en.main: Para 3: the auditor shall obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that provides REASONABLE assurance that the IFI has complied with Shari'a Rules and Principles. Citing ASIFI 1, reasonable assurance also means the auditor is satisfied that the transactions examined comply with Shari'a Rules and Principles AS DETERMINED BY THE SSB of the institution, not by the auditor's own interpretation.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: Following media criticism of a profit-rate swap product, an Islamic bank's board asks who is responsible for ensuring that the bank's activities comply with Shari'a and who interprets the Shari'a Rules and Principles. Which answer is consistent with ASIFI 4?
en.A: Management is responsible for ensuring that the financial statements and activities comply with Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB, and the responsibility to interpret those rules lies with the SSB
en.B: The external auditor is responsible for both ensuring compliance and interpreting Shari'a rules, since he expresses an opinion on the financial statements
en.C: The SSB is responsible for ensuring compliance of all activities, while the external auditor interprets the rules
en.D: The internal audit function is responsible for ensuring compliance, while management interprets the rules
en.True answer: Management is responsible for ensuring that the financial statements and activities comply with Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB, and the responsibility to interpret those rules lies with the SSB
en.main: Para 5: while the auditor forms and expresses an opinion on the financial statements, MANAGEMENT is responsible for ensuring that the financial statements and activities comply with Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSPara 6: as explained in GSIFI No. 1, the responsibility to INTERPRET Shari'a Rules and Principles lies with the SSB.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: Management of an Islamic bank asks the external audit partner to give a formal view on whether a novel Sukuk structure that the bank plans to use is permissible under Shari'a, so that it can be launched before the next SSB meeting. How should the partner respond under ASIFI 4?
en.A: Provide the interpretation, since the auditor is required to be knowledgeable about Shari'a Rules and Principles
en.B: Provide the interpretation, provided it is later ratified by the SSB
en.C: Decline to provide an interpretation, because although the auditor shall be knowledgeable about Shari'a, he is not expected to interpret Shari'a Rules and Principles; this is the role of the SSB
en.D: Provide the interpretation only if the audit firm employs a qualified Shari'a scholar
en.True answer: Decline to provide an interpretation, because although the auditor shall be knowledgeable about Shari'a, he is not expected to interpret Shari'a Rules and Principles; this is the role of the SSB
en.main: Para 7: the auditor shall be knowledgeable about Shari'a Rules and Principles, but would not possess the same level of knowledge as SSB members and therefore shall NOT be expected to provide interpretation of these rules. Para 6: interpretation is the responsibility of the SSPara 11 also requires new products to go through appropriate compliance procedures, including SSB review.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: The audit firm's own Shari'a adviser disagrees with a fatwa issued by an Islamic bank's SSB permitting a particular treatment of late-payment charity. What basis should the external auditor use to conclude whether the bank's financial statements have been prepared in accordance with Shari'a Rules and Principles?
en.A: The opinion of the audit firm's own Shari'a adviser, to safeguard the auditor's independence
en.B: The fatwas, rulings and guidance issued by the bank's own SSB
en.C: The majority opinion of the major schools of Islamic jurisprudence
en.D: The more conservative of the two opinions, to apply prudence
en.True answer: The fatwas, rulings and guidance issued by the bank's own SSB
en.main: Para 8: the fatwas, rulings and guidance issued by the SSB form the basis on which the auditor considers whether the IFI has complied with Shari'a Rules and Principles, and the auditor shall use them as the basis for concluding whether the financial statements have been prepared accordingly. Para 9: the auditor's responsibility is to form an opinion on compliance with the fatwas, rulings and guidance issued by the IFI's SSB.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: At the annual general meeting of an Islamic bank, a shareholder asks the external auditor to state in the auditor's report whether the members of the Shari'a Supervisory Board are sufficiently qualifieUnder ASIFI 4, how should the auditor respond?
en.A: Assess the SSB members' qualifications and include a conclusion in the auditor's report
en.B: Assess the SSB members' qualifications and report only to the board of directors
en.C: Qualify the opinion until the SSB members' competence can be verified
en.D: Explain that the auditor has no responsibility for assessing the competence of the SSB members
en.True answer: Explain that the auditor has no responsibility for assessing the competence of the SSB members
en.main: Para 10: the auditor shall have NO responsibility for assessing the competence of the members of the SSThe auditor's responsibility is to form an opinion on whether transactions comply with the SSB's fatwas, rulings and guidance (para 9).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question:
Which of the following are required procedures for the external auditor under ASIFI 4?
i. Satisfying himself that the IFI's process for introducing new or modified products includes appropriate Shari'a compliance procedures, including reviews by management, internal audit and the SSB
ii. Including procedures to ensure that all new fatwas, rulings and guidance, and modifications to existing ones, are identified and reviewed for each period under examination
iii. Approving each new product before it is presented to the SSB
iv. Verifying, on a test basis, that the transactions entered into by the IFI are consistent with the fatwas, rulings and guidelines of the SSB
en.A: i and ii only
en.B: ii, iii and iv
en.C: i, ii and iv
en.D: i, ii, iii and iv
en.True answer: i, ii and iv
en.main: Para 11 requires (i); para 12 requires (ii); para 14 requires (iv), with the nature and extent of testing determined by the auditor according to the IFI's circumstances. Approving products (iii) is not the auditor's role; product approval rests with the SSB and management (paras 6, 11, 13).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: While reviewing the SSB's minutes of meetings, the external auditor finds no evidence that a recently launched Islamic credit card product was ever reviewed by the SSUnder ASIFI 4, what is the correct view of the auditor's responsibility here?
en.A: As part of his own scope of work, the auditor shall review available documents, including SSB reports and minutes, to ensure all types of products have been reviewed by the SSB and found compliant, and shall consider the effect of these matters on his work
en.B: The matter is outside the auditor's scope, since product approval is the sole responsibility of the SSB
en.C: The auditor should approve the product himself if its contract terms appear consistent with Shari'a
en.D: The auditor need only rely on management's written confirmation that the product is Shari'a-compliant
en.True answer: As part of his own scope of work, the auditor shall review available documents, including SSB reports and minutes, to ensure all types of products have been reviewed by the SSB and found compliant, and shall consider the effect of these matters on his work
en.main: Para 13: as part of his OWN scope of work, the auditor shall review available documents to ensure that all types of products have been reviewed by the SSB in accordance with GSIFI No. 2, and satisfy himself that the SSB found them compliant. Documents include the SSB's reports and minutes of meetings, and the auditor considers their effect on the work to be carried out.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: The internal Shari'a review of an Islamic bank reports that, in one branch, a significant number of Murabaha contracts were signed with customers before the bank had acquired ownership of the goods. How should the external auditor respond under ASIFI 4?*
en.A: Ignore the finding, because the external auditor must perform independent work without regard to internal reviews
en.B: Rely entirely on the internal Shari'a review and perform no further testing in that branch
en.C: Refer the finding to the SSB and suspend the audit until the SSB issues a new fatwa
en.D: Review the finding and consider whether it affects the nature, timing or extent of his own work, for example by expanding the testing of Murabaha transactions
en.True answer: Review the finding and consider whether it affects the nature, timing or extent of his own work, for example by expanding the testing of Murabaha transactions
en.main: Para 15: the auditor shall review the findings of all internal reviews by management, internal audit and the internal Shari'a review (GSIFI No. 3), and consider whether they affect the NATURE, TIMING or EXTENT of his work. Para 14: testing is on a test basis, with nature and extent determined by the auditor according to the IFI's circumstances.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question:
Which of the following statements regarding the interaction between the auditor's report and the SSB's report under ASIFI 4 are correct?
iv. Prior to issuance of the SSB's final report, the auditor shall make available to the SSB his draft report and conclusions related to Shari'a compliance.
iii. The auditor must always issue his final report before the SSB issues its draft report, to preserve independence.
